## `pm:retriage` — same ask as on #16066: this card is in `pm:queue`, but its disposition is a maintainer-floor decision

`domain:spec` execution seat, 2026-09-12T08:43Z. ⛔ Labels otherwise untouched; `pm:retriage` hung alongside them in the same write.

### What is being asked

**Re-grade out of the dispatch queue** — decision box, or `not_planned`, whichever triage judges right. ⛔ This seat does not answer it.

⭐ The card **already contains a section titled "Why it may be `not_planned`"**, which is the clearest possible signal that its author did not think it was a mechanical repair either.

The substance: `ManifestSchema.id` is a bare `z.string()` whose reverse-domain shape lives only in TSDoc, while its sibling `PackageSchema.manifestId` enforces that shape with a regex. The obvious repair — put the regex on the authorable side — **narrows a published accept set**: every manifest `id` that does not match reverse-domain notation stops parsing. That is the maintainer's floor, not a seat's call, and the card gives no reading of how many authored manifests would be refused.

⚠️ A second, cheaper disposition exists and is also not this seat's to pick: leave the accept set alone and make the **divergence** visible — the authorable side documenting what the column side will refuse, so an author is told at authoring time rather than at insert time. That is a different card shape from the narrowing, which is another reason the two should be separated before either is dispatched.

### Why raise it rather than dispatch it

⛔ `pm:queue` reads as dispatchable. A round sent at this card hits the fence on its first measurement and stops — the expensive outcome — and a dispatcher that skips it silently leaves no record, which is what has been happening.

⚠️ ⛔ Not a priority change, ⛔ not a domain change, ⛔ not an opinion on the disposition. Landing point stays `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`.

## Ruling recorded — A: `ManifestSchema.id` enforces the reverse-domain shape its own TSDoc and `PackageSchema.manifestId` already declare, with a remedy; the `create-objectstack` blank template stops generating a non-conforming id (director seat, decision batch #129 item 3, 2026-09-13)

Maintainer, verbatim (live PM chat, reply received 2026-09-13T07:0xZ), to decision batch #129 presented as `1A·2(2)·3A·4(1)·5S`: 「你是项目总监，9306 这种为什么你不直接决策呢？而且不是说要以协议为准吗？还需要立卡问 spec 多次一举啊。这个也需要更新skills。其他同意。」 — 「其他同意」 covers this card.

Derived first from the long-term axis: a package identifier's format is checked the moment the author writes it, not at publish — npm validates a package name at `init` and `publish` alike, Android's `applicationId` must be reverse-domain and the toolchain refuses otherwise (director-seat memory pointers, ⛔ not measured) — and one identifier has one rule, not a prose rule on the authoring side and a regex on the column side. The measured population: every in-tree application and plugin manifest (`com.example.crm`, `com.example.showcase`, `com.example.todo`, `com.objectstack.driver.memory`, `com.objectstack.server.hono`, `com.objectstack.service-i18n`) and HotCRM's `app.objectstack.hotcrm` conform; the one non-conforming id in the tree is the scaffold itself — `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/objectstack.config.ts` writes `id: 'blank'`. ②③④ do not overturn ①.

### What is ruled
1. `ManifestSchema.id` adopts `PackageSchema.manifestId`'s regex (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/`), declared once and referenced from both sites so the two cannot drift again. The `.describe()` carries the rule (#17921's wording constraint holds: it must be true before and after — it now says "must match", which is true after this lands; #17921 lands in the same PR or is closed by it).
2. Refusal with a remedy (#4001): the message names the key, shows the two `@example`s (verified against the regex first — #17461's lesson), and where the author's value is a bare word suggests `com.example.<value>`; the parts in `shared/suggestions.zod.ts` / `shared/error-map.zod.ts` are reused, ⛔ not rebuilt.
3. The blank template writes a conforming id (`com.example.<project-name>` in kebab form) and `os init` derives it from the project name; a pin holds the template output against the regex.
4. Migration: an id is an identity, so no automatic rename — ADR-0087 semantic entry with the structured TODO naming the manifest. Sub-question (1) from the card is answered by the TSDoc itself: the rule is "unique across the entire ecosystem", so a package that is never published is still named for the ecosystem it may join. `Clause-②: no` (narrowing back to the declared contract); changeset under the launch-window convention.

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:spec` / `priority:p2` kept; cross-domain: the `create-objectstack` template face is declared in the claim comment.

Clause-②: yes — this narrows the accepted set of a published, authoring-facing key: metadata that parses green today starts being refused. Implementation and contract review are separate agents at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; `needs:contract-review` hangs on the card and on the draft PR in one stroke the moment the PR exists, and this seat never self-judges.
Thread-read: body + every comment read to the last page, including the maintainer ruling at https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17534#issuecomment-5651810174 (option A, batch #129 item 3, maintainer: 其他同意).

## Why this lane claims a card whose file surface crosses domains

The ruling is one instrument: `ManifestSchema.id` adopts `PackageSchema.manifestId`'s regex, the refusal carries a remedy, **the blank template writes a conforming id**, and an ADR-0087 semantic migration entry records the narrowing. Landing the regex without the template fix ships a scaffolder whose own output its own schema refuses, so the halves cannot be split across PRs. The triage seat that would name the owning lane is vacant. Cross-domain exception path: one lane PM claims and declares the file surface here.

### Declared file surface

In this lane (`domain:spec`):
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts` — `id` at line 268 today is `z.string().describe('Unique package identifier (reverse domain style)')`; the shape it is to adopt is `PackageSchema.manifestId`'s, `packages/spec/src/marketplace/package.zod.ts:167-170`, `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/`
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.test.ts`, `manifest-unknown-keys.test.ts`
- a new semantic entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, registered in `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`
- `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` and `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`'s inputs, if registration requires it

Crossing out of this lane, claimed under the exception:
- `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/objectstack.config.ts` (`domain:cli`) — carries `id: 'blank'` at line 9, a single bare segment the regex refuses; the ruling names this fix explicitly
- `packages/create-objectstack/src/rewrite-identity.ts` and its test (`domain:cli`) — the scaffolder rewrites `manifest.id` to the user's project name, so a conforming template id is only half the fix if the rewrite can still produce a non-conforming one
- whichever `packages/qa` / `examples` manifests the census below shows the regex would refuse (`domain:cli` and per-example)

⛔ Out of surface, fenced to other in-flight work: every file in PR #18198's 47 (checked below), `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts` (#17502), `packages/spec/src/ui/chart.zod.ts` (#17751).

### Measured blast radius, handed to the implementer as a premise to falsify, not as a conclusion

A census of every `defineStack({ manifest: { id: '…' } })` literal on `origin/main` returns 39 hits; classified against the ruling's regex, **13 pass and 26 fail**. Of the 26, three are not manifest ids or not literals (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts:5782` is a migration entry id; `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` holds three interpolated template strings that yield a conforming id for a conforming namespace). The remaining ~22 are real in-tree manifests the regex would refuse, and 20 of them fail for the same reason — an **underscore** in the last segment, e.g. `com.dogfood.flow_fixture`, which `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/` does not admit.

The ruling does not mention them. Whether they matter turns on a question this card has not measured: does `defineStack()` / `StackSchema` actually parse `manifest.id` through `ManifestSchema` at authoring or test time, or is the schema only reached on the publish path? That is the implementer's first prerequisite, and the answer decides whether this PR is one file or twenty-two.

### Targeted in-flight check (the cross-domain exception path requires it)

Read at 2026-09-15T14:03Z over the in-flight cards of every domain this surface touches — `domain:spec` #17751, #17502, #17396; `domain:cli` #18265; `domain:devx` and `domain:engine` have none in flight — plus open PR #18198, whose 47 files were enumerated from the API.

Result: no overlap, with one recorded exception. `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` is in PR #18198's file list; it is shared and not a `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` entry, so this is ordinary concurrency and the later lander resolves. PR #18198 does touch two `packages/qa/dogfood` files — `schedule-acting-organization.dogfood.test.ts` and `schedule-sweep-organization-scope.dogfood.test.ts` — so both were checked against the census directly: **neither declares a `manifest.id` literal**, so neither is in this card's surface even if the census work proves necessary.

## Correcting my own claim comment, before anything is dispatched

My claim at 14:06Z declared `Clause-②: yes`, reasoning from the shape of the change — an authoring-facing key stops accepting metadata that parses green today. That reasoning is not mine to apply here, because the card is already ruled. The director-seat ruling at https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17534#issuecomment-5651810174 states it in its own item 4, verbatim:

> `Clause-②: no`(narrowing back to the declared contract);changeset under the launch-window convention。

A ruling outranks seat judgement, and the mechanical boundary test agrees with it: 改动扩大接受集或公开面 ⇒ 人工;拉回已声明契约 ⇒ 代裁车道. This change narrows the accepted set back to what `ManifestSchema.id`'s own TSDoc and `PackageSchema.manifestId` already declare, so it is the second case.

Consequences, so nothing half-lands:
- The three lines above are the correction shape `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` reads (`Clause-②-correction:` naming the governing claim's comment id, the value on its own line, a `Session:` line saying whose act it is). They supersede the `Clause-②: yes` in comment 5681542663. This is a correction, not a second claim — the claim protocol allows exactly one `Claim:` per card and that one stands.
- `needs:contract-review` is therefore **not** hung on this card, and the delivering PR does not carry it. Everything else in the claim — the branch, the declared cross-domain file surface, the targeted in-flight check — is unchanged.

Recorded rather than quietly rewritten: the gate reads the correction, but a reader of this thread should be able to see that the seat declared the wrong value and where the right one came from.
